video_title: He Lost $14M to FTX. Now He’s Putting Real Stocks on Solana | Armani Ferrante (Backpack)
gist: Backpack CEO Armani Ferrante (ex-Alameda, lost ~90% of capital in FTX) explains Backpack's 1:1 redeemable tokenized equities on Solana, which he says enable Nasdaq-Solana arbitrage and up to 45x better pricing than Robinhood's debt-security tokens, plus its compliance-first single global order book (48% of world GDP), US CFTC applications, the SEC tokenized-venue sandbox's volume limits, and BP tokenomics with insider tokens locked until 1 year post-IPO.

insights.claim: Backpack wraps a bona fide security entitlement in a new security that is 1:1 redeemable for the underlying stock, positioning it between transfer-agent/DTCC models and Robinhood-style debt-security tokens.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Structural differentiation in tokenized stocks: real equity claim plus DeFi composability.
insights.quote: we've taken the bonafide security entitlement, we've wrapped it in a new security, but that security is one-to-one redeemable for the underlying stock

insights.claim: Ferrante maps tokenized stock models on a spectrum: transfer agent models (Superstate, tZERO owned by Bullish) are the canonical ownership record but closed-loop (KYC, whitelisted wallets) and do not fit DeFi AMMs like Raydium or Orca.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Transfer-agent tokenization is 'most real' but lacks DeFi liquidity; different end-markets for each model.
insights.quote: it doesn't fit into the form factor of DeFi markets that exist today

insights.claim: Robinhood's tokenized stocks are structured as an SPV fund issuing a cash-settled debt security tracking the stock, so holders cannot transfer them into a Fidelity account and moving between DeFi and TradFi triggers a taxable sell/buy.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Highlights competitor weakness: debt-security wrappers lack TradFi portability and create tax friction.
insights.quote: ultimately it's a cash settled instrument, so you're going into cash and then from cash you're going in back into the stock and so that's a taxable event

insights.claim: Because anyone can mint and redeem Backpack's tokenized securities, arbitrageurs buy on Nasdaq and sell on Solana when DeFi prices diverge, and Ferrante says each Solana token listing of a Backpack stock brings 10x more volume and liquidity.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Open mint/redeem arbitrage is the mechanism behind liquidity and tighter pricing; a moat if competitors can't replicate.
insights.quote: every time you see a token listing on Solana, and for any one of our stocks, you see 10x more volume, 10x more liquidity

insights.claim: Citing a Blockworks analysis, Ferrante claims buyers sometimes get up to 45x better pricing on Backpack securities on Solana than on Robinhood's tokenized stocks on Robinhood chain.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Execution-quality gap is a key competitive metric in tokenized equities; Solana venue vs Robinhood chain.
insights.quote: in some cases, you actually get 45 times better pricing when buying Backpack securities on Solana than you would buying the Robinhood tokenized stocks on Robinhood chain

insights.claim: Users can buy a stock such as SpaceX on Solana and transfer it into a Fidelity or Interactive Brokers account, and on-ramp the reverse direction into a self-custodial wallet.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: TradFi-DeFi portability of equities, including private-ish names like SpaceX, broadens demand base.
insights.quote: I could buy stock on SpaceX today on Solana and go and transfer it into my Fidelity account

insights.claim: Ferrante claims Backpack is the first and, to his knowledge, the only product offering 1:1 redeemable tokenized equity that moves freely between brokerage and DeFi.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: First-mover claim worth verifying against competitors.
insights.quote: we're the first in the world to do this and till this day as far as I'm aware, the only product on the market that gives you this functionality

insights.claim: Ferrante likens Backpack's tokenized stocks to stablecoins (open-loop, instant settlement) and DTCC/transfer-agent tokenization to bank deposit tokens, which he calls valuable infrastructure that will make brokers and banks 10x more efficient but which few people use.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Suggests the open-loop issuer model wins retail/DeFi adoption, while closed-loop models serve institutions.
insights.quote: Backpack is really like the true stablecoin model

insights.claim: The main trade-off of Backpack's model is issuer counterparty risk, comparable to trusting Circle or Tether not to get hacked and to manage capital prudently.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Key risk for holders of issuer-based tokenized stocks: issuer solvency and security.
insights.quote: really the tradeoff that you're making is you're taking on counterparty risk

insights.claim: All stablecoin-style tokenized stock models, including Backpack's, currently operate outside the US and are not available to US users.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: US access is the next big unlock and a regulatory overhang for the whole category.
insights.quote: they're all outside of the US right now

insights.claim: In DeFi, dividends on Backpack tokenized stocks accrue in kind (e.g., 1 Apple share becoming 1.01 shares), while cash dividends, voting rights and corporate actions are available by moving the token into the brokerage.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Operational detail on corporate actions; in-kind accrual keeps tokens DeFi-compatible.
insights.quote: you might have 1.01 shares of Apple stock when you wake up the next morning

insights.claim: Weekend price discovery for Backpack's tokenized stocks comes only from on-chain spot markets and perps since traditional venues are closed, and Ferrante estimates upwards of 80% of volume happens over the weekend.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Demand for 24/7 equity exposure is strong; weekend on-chain trading may become a price-discovery venue.
insights.quote: I want to say upwards towards 80% of the volumes happening over the weekend

insights.claim: Where perps exist on a tokenized stock, they lead off-hours price discovery, mirroring how perps lead Bitcoin pricing, though many symbols have no perps yet.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Equity perps could become the after-hours benchmark; opportunity for venues listing them.
insights.quote: on Bitcoin, you know, the perps generally lead, you know, pricing, and so I think you're seeing a similar structure emerge

insights.claim: Ferrante says there have been days when Backpack's tokenized stock volume on Solana exceeded Nasdaq's 24-hour trading volume (likely for specific symbols/overnight session).
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Signals material tokenized equity volume, at least for select symbols.
insights.quote: there's already been days when we've surpassed Nasdaq's 24 trading volume on Solana

insights.claim: Perpetual futures are the most important crypto product after stablecoins, doing hundreds of billions in volume with price discovery fully offshore on unregulated venues; bringing them onshore to the US is in the 'first inning' and a key pillar of the next growth wave.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Onshore US perps (Kalshi, Coinbase, Kraken) are a major structural growth driver for regulated venues.
insights.quote: the single most important product in crypto outside of stablecoins in the perp

insights.claim: Ferrante sees the 24/7 trading era as either here or imminent, driven by global demand.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Supports thesis on round-the-clock equity markets and venues positioned for it.
insights.quote: the 24/7 era is if it's not here, it's definitely coming

themes.theme: US regulatory shift and SEC tokenized-venue sandbox

insights.claim: Ferrante describes a 180-degree shift to the most pro-free-market US regulatory environment ever, with deeply knowledgeable agency staff, though the CLARITY Act stalling is a disappointment.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Regulatory tailwind for US crypto market structure; legislative risk around CLARITY.
insights.quote: clarity is kind of a bummer to see that stall out and hopefully gets revitalized

insights.claim: Backpack has public CFTC applications across the full spectrum: DCO (clearing house), DCM (market) and FCM (broker).
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Backpack aims to become a fully regulated US derivatives venue; watch approvals.
insights.quote: There's, you know, the clearing house, the DCO, the markets and the DCM, and obviously the FCM

insights.claim: The SEC's innovation exemption sandbox for tokenized trading venues (TSVs) on public blockchains is 'crawl, walk, run' and not ready for scale due to limits on volume, symbols and token types; Backpack plans to join, a question of when.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Sandbox is a concrete signal tokenized markets are coming to the US but V1 is constrained.
insights.quote: what this sandbox is is it's the initial test flight to legalize tokenized trading venues on public blockchains

insights.claim: Under V1 sandbox rules, a TSV must circuit-break if its volume exceeds roughly 20bps of the primary venue's volume (Ferrante's uncertain recollection), so Backpack's Solana stock volume is already too big to bring into that structure.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Volume caps limit how much tokenized trading can move onshore via the sandbox in the near term.
insights.quote: I think it's something on the order of of 20 bips of the relative volume of the primary trading venue

themes.theme: Backpack's global licensing strategy and business mix

insights.claim: Backpack's product is available in about 48% of the world by GDP, after a multi-year country-by-country licensing plan starting with a Dubai license, 3 years in Europe and roughly 4 years each on Japan and the US.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Licensing footprint is the moat in compliance-first exchange strategy; remaining 52% is upside.
insights.quote: today the product is in about 48% of the world if you measure by GDP

insights.claim: Backpack says it has completed the 'holy trinity' of licensing in Europe across spot and derivatives, payments/fiat rails and equities.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: European full-stack licensing enables cross-asset product there.
insights.quote: we've kind of finished the let's call it the holy trinity of licensure there

insights.claim: Unlike competitors that run separate entities per jurisdiction, Backpack is building a single globally regulated system with one order book and unified cross-margined liquidity across crypto and traditional asset classes.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Unified global liquidity, if achieved, is a structural edge over fragmented exchange models.
insights.quote: A single system, single order book, single liquidity across margined, across all asset classes

insights.claim: Backpack's business is led by perps and margin trading, with tokenized stocks the fastest-growing segment; the host cites 450 billion in cumulative volume and daily volume regularly above 1 billion.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante / host
insights.so_what: Tokenized stocks are the growth vector; scale indicators for valuation.
insights.quote: Tokenized stocks is definitely the fastest growing segment right now

insights.claim: Ferrante claims Backpack is essentially the only exchange that took a compliance-first approach instead of opening to the whole world on day one, including daily published proof of reserves.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Compliance-first positioning may win institutional and regulated-market share post-FTX.
insights.quote: we're really the only one that took this compliance-oriented approach where we did not just open up our product to the entire world on day one

insights.claim: Backpack's long-term vision includes users anywhere (e.g., Brazil via Pix) buying stocks, trading derivatives, accessing DeFi and sending money in one regulated app.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Emerging-market retail access to US equities is a large TAM.

themes.theme: BP token design and IPO aspiration

insights.claim: No BP token warrants were ever given to founders, board, executives, investors or staff; company-held tokens are locked until one year after an IPO or similar equity exit.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Unusual tokenomics reduces insider sell pressure on BP.
insights.quote: those tokens are locked 1 year post IPO

insights.claim: Ferrante argues crypto's TGE market structure (exchange hype, day-one FDV Polymarket markets, 'institutional farms') makes tokens an exit event where retail becomes exit liquidity and charts bleed to zero.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward TGE-driven tokens; favors projects with long-dated insider locks.
insights.quote: it's always the retail user holding the bag that is the exit liquidity

insights.claim: Ferrante frames tokens as the most powerful incentive tool for bootstrapping network effects but the worst incentive for building durable companies, due to current market structure rather than tokens per se.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Lens for evaluating token designs: bootstrapping vs long-term alignment.
insights.quote: tokens are the most powerful incentive tool ever created

insights.claim: BP stakers were allocated 20% of the company's equity as of TGE, convertible post-IPO subject to normal dilution, with a real-time share emission schedule.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Token-to-equity conversion creates a quasi-equity claim on Backpack.
insights.quote: it was 20% on the day of TGE

insights.claim: Backpack aims to IPO but will not do so this year and offers no guarantee it ever will.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: No near-term IPO catalyst for BP equity conversion.
insights.quote: We're not going to IP IPO this year

insights.claim: Backpack had about 88-90% of its capital on FTX when it collapsed, a loss the host puts at over 14 million, effectively killing the company before it pivoted.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Founder resilience and origin of compliance-first strategy.
insights.quote: we had 88, close to 90% of our capital on FTX at the time of the collapse

insights.claim: Ferrante, an early Alameda engineer and creator of Solana's Anchor framework, says the FTX collapse was formative: crypto exchanges are among the most security-critical systems, and 'what rises fast also falls just as fast'.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Informs a lower-risk operational posture for an exchange investment.
insights.quote: what rises fast also falls just as fast

insights.claim: Ferrante remains a Solana maximalist on liquidity, applications and foundation leadership (Anatoly, Raj, Lily), though Backpack supports every chain.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Solana as primary venue for tokenized equities.
insights.quote: Come for the tech, stay for the vibes
